subject: The teaching and the sangha
place: The Ganges plain — villages and kingdoms
events: The Buddha walks the roads of the Ganges plain for forty-five years
He teaches kings and outcasts alike
His quiet victory over the mind spreads the teaching
grounding_notes: The path is open to all, as the river is open to all who would drink.
The sangha is the company of those who walk together.
The victory is over the mind, not over enemies.
A lamp does not hide its own light.
contemporary_mapping: The modern question of meaning — finding nobility in compassion and service rather than status.

included_characters.role_in_chapter: Protagonist — the Buddha who teaches the path

chapter_summary: For forty-five years the Buddha walks the roads of the Ganges plain, teaching all who will listen — kings and beggars, merchants and outcasts, men and women alike. He founds the sangha, the community of monks and nuns, and teaches compassion, loving-kindness, the middle way, and the discipline of the mind. A king asks what the greatest gift is, and the Buddha answers: the gift of the teaching. An outcast asks if he is too low to walk the path, and the Buddha answers: the path is open to all. His victory is a quiet one — over the mind's craving, aversion, and delusion — and the teaching spreads across the world.
